package.name: P2D1
package.description:
COMPSCI 603 Project 2 Deliverable 1: Manual Q-table wall following
This package implements a LiDAR-based wall-following controller for the Triton robot in Gazebo using a manually specified Q-table policy.
The controller uses LiDAR measurements from the front of the robot and divides them into three non-overlapping angular sectors:
Front-Right (FR) Front (F) Front-Left (FL)
These sectors are separated by angular gaps to reduce the impact of sensor noise.
The controller uses a discretized state defined as:
state = (FR_distance_bin, Front_flag)
FR_distance_bin ∈ {TOO_CLOSE, CLOSE, DW, FAR} Front_flag ∈ {BLOCKED, CLEAR}
The controller selects one of the following motion primitives:
FWD_FAST FWD_SLOW TURN_L_SOFT TURN_R_SOFT TURN_L_HARD TURN_R_HARD
Each action corresponds to a fixed linear and angular velocity command, specifically defined in p2d1.launch.
The controller selects the action with the maximum Q-value such that:
If the robot is too far from the wall, it steers toward it. If the robot is too close to the wall, it steers away. If an obstacle is detected in front, it performs a stronger turn to avoid collision. Otherwise the robot moves forward while maintaining the desired wall distance.
This package requires the stingray_sim package, so ensure stingray_sim is located inside the same catkin workspace before building.
Commands to run the demonstration:
cd ~/catkin_ws catkin_make source devel/setup.bash roslaunch P2D1 p2d1.launch
The controller publishes velocity commands to /cmd_vel and the robot follows the wall on its right side while maintaining approximately the desired distance d_w.
